correctness.rationale: Exact marked-block enumeration yields three Stirling identities. The conditional zero-truncated Poisson representation and a local analytic saddle-point expansion with uniform second derivatives yield the Schur-complement covariance. Its sign reduces to h_j(x); strict convexity of h_j(x)/x proves one root for j>=3, derivative monotonicity handles j=2, and a strictly increasing j(x) proves threshold ordering. Finite RGS enumeration independently checks the exact moments; it is not substituted for the all-n proof. No critical-ray claim.

value.rationale: Fixed total block count is a basic constraint in random clustering/assemblies. The sign of association between singleton prevalence and j-sized groups is not determined by individual marginal moment laws. The theorem shows nontrivial emergence of positive covariance for every j>=3 at large block density, while j=2 is always negative to leading order, and classifies every fixed-size threshold with monotone hierarchy and a natural reciprocal-size scaling. This is a substantive probabilistic dependence phenomenon beyond a routine numerical table.
